builder_plan.scenario: A narrow, repeated product task may not need your largest model.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a released student model fits the task before generating training data.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current model and an off-the-shelf small model on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Student quality, serving cost, teacher calls, training cost, and failures on unusual inputs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MeanVoiceFlow2: Joint Optimization of Mean Flow and Content Encoder for Fast One-Step Zero-Shot Voice Conversion
summary: The method replaces the computationally intensive content encoder and multi-step flow inference of MeanVoiceFlow with a jointly optimized lightweight content encoder and one-step conversion module trained via conversion distillation, real-data reconstruction, and diffusion-GAN training with sample mixing. The cost is a full training pipeline requiring a MeanVoiceFlow teacher, training data, GAN-based optimization, and implementation effort, plus possible quality risks that the paper's metrics may not capture for a given voice domain. Adoption can fail if the teacher model or training data licenses are unavailable, if GAN/distillation training proves unstable for the team's target speakers, or if the zero-shot similarity degrades on out-of-distribution voices.
rationale: The 9x inference speedup suits a single 24 GB GPU for production voice conversion, but the method requires a distillation-and-GAN training pipeline whose feasibility and quality must be validated on the team's own data before production use.
technique: Joint flow-matching and content-encoder distillation for one-step voice conversion
